claim: Acute stress increased hippocampal cell proliferation in adult rats.
source_text: We found that acute stress increased hippocampal cell proliferation and astrocytic fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) expression.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of cell proliferation in the hippocampus following acute stress exposure, as detailed in the Results section with Ki67+ and BrdU+ cell counts.

claim: Acute stress increased astrocytic fibroblast growth factor 2 (FGF2) expression.

claim: The effect of acute stress on hippocampal cell proliferation occurred independent of basolateral amygdala neural input.
source_text: The effect of acute stress occurred independent of basolateral amygdala neural input and was mimicked by treating isolated NPCs with conditioned media from corticosterone-treated primary astrocytes.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from BLA lesion studies showing that stress-induced proliferation persisted even after BLA lesioning.

claim: Astrocyte-secreted FGF2 mediated stress-hormone-induced NPC proliferation.
source_text: Neutralization of FGF2 revealed that astrocyte-secreted FGF2 mediated stress-hormone-induced NPC proliferation.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that FGF2 neutralizing antibody blocked the proliferative effect of conditioned media from CORT-treated astrocytes on NPCs.

claim: 2 weeks after acute stress, rats showed enhanced fear extinction memory.
source_text: 2 weeks, but not 2 days, after acute stress, rats also showed enhanced fear extinction memory coincident with enhanced activation of newborn neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by behavioral data showing reduced freezing in immobilized rats during the 24-hr extinction probe at the 2-week timepoint.

claim: 2 weeks after acute stress, rats showed enhanced activation of newborn neurons.

claim: Brief stress has a beneficial role for the hippocampus.
source_text: Our findings suggest a beneficial role for brief stress on the hippocampus and improve understanding of the adaptive capacity of the brain.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the combined findings of increased neurogenesis and enhanced memory performance following acute stress.

claim: Moderate stress enhances memory performance in rodents while more severe stress impairs it.
